'''Albert Folch Folch''' ({{IPAc-en|f|oʊ|k}} {{respell|FOHK}}; born September 25, 1966) is a Spanish/Catalan scientist, writer, and artist. He is the son of editor Xavier Folch[https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Folch_i_Recasens] and sinologist Dolors Folch[https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolors_Folch_i_Fornesa]. He is currently a [[professor]] in the Department of [[Bioengineering]] at the [[University of Washington]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://depts.washington.edu/bioe/portfolio-items/folch/|title=Faculty and Staff: Albert Folch|work=UW Bioengineering |publisher=Department of Bioengineering, [[University of Washington]]|access-date=2015-11-25}}</ref> who is known for his research into [[Microfluidics]] and [[BioMEMS]] as well as his works of scientific art.

==Background==
Folch received his B.Sc. in Physics from the [[University of Barcelona]] (U.B.) in 1989. In 1994, he received his Ph.D. in [[Surface Science]] and [[Nanotechnology]] from the U.B.'s Physics Dept. under Javier Tejada's supervision. During his Ph.D. he was also a visiting scientist (1990–91) at the [[Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]] ([[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], California) working on [[atomic force microscopy]] under Miquel Salmeron. From 1994 to 1996, he was a postdoc at [[M.I.T.]] developing microdevices under the advice of [[Martin A. Schmidt]] (EECS Dept.) and [[Mark S. Wrighton]] (Chemistry). In 1997, he joined the laboratory of [[Mehmet Toner]] as a postdoc at [[Harvard University]]'s Center for Engineering in Medicine to work on [[BioMEMS]] and [[Tissue Engineering]]. In 2000 he joined the [[University of Washington]]'s Dept. of [[Bioengineering]] ([[Seattle]]), where he is a full professor. In 2001 he received a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=NSF Award Search: Award # 0094035 - CAREER: Micron-Scale Engineering of Cellular Environments|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0094035&HistoricalAwards=false|access-date=2022-02-01|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref> and in 2014 he was elected to the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] (AIMBE) College of Fellows Class of 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wright|first=Laura Elizabeth|url=http://depts.washington.edu/bioe/suzie-pun-albert-folch-aimbe-2015/|title=Suzie Pun, Albert Folch inducted as 2015 AIMBE Fellows|publisher=Department of Bioengineering, University of Washington|date=2015-03-24|access-date=2015-11-25}}</ref> In 2022, he was elected Corresponding Member of the Science&Technology Section of the [[Institute for Catalan Studies]] (''Institut d’Estudis Catalans'', Catalonia, Spain),<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> one of highest honors bestowed upon Catalan scientists. He has served on the [[advisory board]] of the BioMEMS journal ''[[Lab on a Chip (journal)|Lab on a Chip]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pubs.rsc.org/en/Journals/JournalIssues/LC |title=''Lab on a Chip'' website |publisher=Pubs.rsc.org |date= |access-date=2011-10-25}}</ref> since 2006 and on the editorial boards of ''Technology'' and ''Micromachines'' since 2013 and 2019, respectively.

==Scientific research and teaching==
The Folch Lab<ref>{{cite web|url=http://faculty.washington.edu/afolch |title=Folch Lab Homepage |publisher=Faculty.washington.edu |date= |access-date=2011-10-25}}</ref> works on the interface between [[microfluidics]] and [[cancer]]. The lab develops microfluidic devices to test multiple cancer drugs on a small, live, intact tumor biopsy at high fidelity in order to help doctors decide which drug is most efficacious. The lab also develops [[3D printing]] approaches to make microfluidic devices as easy to use as [[smartphones]] and make them easily available to clinicians in order to enable novel cancer diagnostics and therapies.  

As part of the undergraduate and graduate curriculum of the University of Washington's Bioengineering Department, Folch has taught a course on [[BioMEMS]]<ref>{{cite web|author=Albert Folch |url=http://courses.washington.edu/bioen455 |title=Link to BioMEMS course taught by Albert Folch |publisher=Courses.washington.edu |date= |access-date=2011-10-25}}</ref> from 2001-2024 that led to his textbook ''Introduction to BioMEMS'' ([[CRC Press]], 2012)<ref name="textbook" /> and a course on Cancer Biosensors since 2015.

==Artistic activity==
The Folch Lab produces microscopy images of microchannels and cells that it then uses to run an artistic outreach program called "BAIT", short for "Bringing Art Into Technology".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://faculty.washington.edu/afolch/FolchLabART.html |title=Folch Lab ART Webpage |publisher=Faculty.washington.edu |date= |access-date=2011-10-25}}</ref> The micrographs act as ''baits'' to entice people to read the accompanying texts (the science) displayed next to the images. Hence, the visitors of the exhibit enjoy the art and leave having learned some science via an artistic experience. While a few of the micrographs are exhibited as obtained by the students without much modification, most pieces are collages, mosaics, and/or mixed-media montages (containing actual devices) made by Folch. However, Folch considers each piece a "collaboration" between him and his students (who are always credited by name, as in a scientific publication).
 
BAIT now consists of a free online gallery<ref>{{Cite web|title=Picture Galleries|url=https://albertfolch.wixsite.com/folchlabhome/picasa-gallery|access-date=2022-02-01|website=folchlabhome|language=en}}</ref> (with more than 1,000 images), a YouTube channel,<ref>{{Cite web|title=folchlab - YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/user/folchlab|access-date=2022-02-01|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref> and more than 60 printed or framed pieces. BAIT has produced six major exhibits. The largest exhibit<ref>{{cite web|url=https://picasaweb.google.com/102864211467583145284/BAITExhibitUWResearchCommons# |title=Folch Lab Exhibit at UW Allen Library |date=2010-11-10 |access-date=2011-10-25}}</ref> was at the University of Washington's [[University of Washington Libraries|Allen Library]] in 2010. In 2013, BAIT was exhibited in the halls of the 2013 [[Biomedical Engineering Society]] meeting in the [[Seattle Convention Center]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://picasaweb.google.com/102864211467583145284/BAITExhibitBMES2013# |title=Folch Lab Exhibit at 2013 BMES meeting|date=2013-10-30 |access-date=2013-10-30}}</ref> In 2014, six pieces from BAIT were exhibited during the Mahato Memorial at [[Duke University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2AUzQG-R6SI |title=Mahato Memorial- BAIT presentation by Albert Folch|publisher=YouTube |date=2014-11-28 |access-date=2014-11-28}}</ref> the first time that BAIT was invited outside of Seattle. BAIT has been featured twice on TV ([[UWTV]] in January 2012 <ref name=UWTV>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7b-C4Q6sj1M|title=Link to UWTV feature program on BAIT |website=[[YouTube]] |date=2012-01-10 |access-date=2013-11-20}}</ref> and [[NTN24]] in November 2014 <ref name=NTN24>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HuMwtElyCRY|title=Link to NTN24 Interview by Luis Quevedo |website=[[YouTube]] |date=2014-11-25 |access-date=2014-11-25}}</ref>).

Folch's artistic activity extends into graphic design. He has designed the logo for the University of Washington's Bioengineering Department and Folch Lab's art has been used in a number of brochures of scientific venues.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://albertfolch.wix.com/folchlabhome#!picasa-gallery/cim8 |title=Brochures designed by the Folch Lab |work=folchlabhome |publisher=Folch Lab |date= |access-date=2014-06-15}}</ref>

==Literary activity==
Folch has written a total of six books, comprising two general science books in Catalan (translated titles: ''Caught on the Internet'' and ''The Science in Soccer''), a textbook in English (''Introduction to BioMEMS''), a book about soccer in English (''For the Love of the Ball''), a microfluidics book in English (''Hidden In Plain Sight - The History, Science, and Engineering of Microfluidic Technology''), and a general-public microfluidics book also in English (''How the World Flows - Microfluidics from Raindrops to Covid Tests'')''.''

* ''Caught on the Internet'' (Editorial Empuries, 1997)<ref>{{Cite book|last=Folch|first=Albert|title=Atrapats a Internet|publisher=Editorial Empuries|year=1997|isbn=978-8475965246|location=Barcelona|language=Catalan}}</ref> teaches what the Internet is about to computer-illiterate audiences, starting from bits and bytes and ending with issues such as social fairness and hackers. This book is in its second edition and an extract of it is used in a textbook for Catalan middle schoolers.
* ''The Science in Soccer'' (Editorial Empuries, 2004)<ref>{{Cite book|last=Folch|first=Albert|title=La Ciencia del Futbol|publisher=Editorial Empuries|year=2004|isbn=978-8497870467|location=Barcelona, Spain|language=Catalan}}</ref> uses soccer examples to convey science. The book is organized in chapters related to various soccer subjects ("The ball", "The field", "The player", etc.). Inside each chapter we find the answers to questions such as what it would be like to play soccer in each of the planets of the Solar System, why the ball is more than one meter ahead of where we think it really is in a 100&nbsp;km/h kick (due to delays in the transmission of the nervous impulse), or why soccer balls are made of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons, etc. Folch has used examples from this book to give outreach lectures to high-schools, middle-schools and elementary schools.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Anderson|first=Charles|date=2017-02-15|title=AMN8 Queenstown: teaching science through a soccer ball, with a dash of apocalypse|url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/partner/amn8-2017/15-02-2017/amn8-queenstown-teaching-science-through-a-soccer-ball-with-a-dash-of-apocalypse|access-date=2022-02-01|website=The Spinoff}}</ref>
* ''Introduction to BioMEMS'' (CRC Press, 2012)<ref name="textbook">{{cite web|url=http://www.crcpress.com/product/isbn/9781439818398 |title=Link to Albert Folch's textbook, "Introduction to BioMEMS", published by CRC Press (528 pages) |publisher= CRC Press |date=2012-03-15 |access-date=2012-04-27}}</ref> covers the whole breadth of [[Bio-MEMS]] (Biomedical MicroElectroMechanicalSystems), including classical microfabrication, microfluidics, tissue engineering, cell-based and non-cell-based devices, and implantable systems. This textbook has now been adopted worldwide (~100 departments in 18 countries).<ref name="wix">{{cite web|url=http://albertfolch.wix.com/introtobiomems |title=Link to Albert Folch's textbook webpage |work=Introduction to BioMEMS website |access-date=2015-10-22}}</ref>
* ''For the Love of the Ball'' (Amazon, 2013)<ref name="soccerbook">{{cite book|last1=Folch |first1=Albert |title=Link to Albert Folch's book on FC Barcelona's youth academy, "For the Love of the Ball" |date=2013-10-20 |publisher=CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform |isbn = 978-1492924272}}</ref> tells the history and methods of FC Barcelona's youth academy. Folch kept a related blog site during 2014-2017, titled ''La Ciencia del Fútbol'',<ref name="blogsite">{{cite web|url=http://afolch.blogspot.com|title=Link to Albert Folch's blogsite, "La Ciencia del Fútbol" (afolch.blogspot.com) |date=2014-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-01}}</ref> where he talked about FC Barcelona's state of affairs with a scientific perspective.
* ''Hidden In Plain Sight'' (MIT Press, 2022)<ref>{{Cite book|last=Folch|first=Albert|url=https://mitpress.mit.edu/books/hidden-plain-sight-1|title=Hidden in Plain Sight: The History, Science, and Engineering of Microfluidic Technology|date=2022-04-12|publisher=MIT Press|isbn=978-0-262-04689-3|location=Cambridge, MA, USA|language=en}}</ref> describes the development and use of key microfluidic devices, explaining not only the technology but also the efforts, teams, places, and circumstances that enabled these inventions.
* ''How the World Flows'' ([[Oxford University Press]], 2025)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/how-the-world-flows-9780197772829?cc=us&lang=en&|title=How the World Flows|date=29 November 2025|access-date=29 November 2025|website=Oxford University Press|last=OUP}}</ref> acts like a microscope that pulls the reader into the barely noticeable, Lilliputian world of fluids at small scales--the microfluidic world-and answers the question "What is microfluidics?" in non-technical language.

Folch also created a large Catalan Poetry Selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lletra.uoc.edu/especials/folch/index.html |title=Selection of Catalan Poetry by Albert Folch |publisher=Lletra.uoc.edu |date= |access-date=2011-10-25}}</ref> This webpage, originally hosted by [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|M.I.T.]] and manually typed in 1995 just one year after the World Wide Web started, was, at the time, the first online literary resource of its kind and size in any language. Still widely visited, the selection features 800 poems and 176 Catalan poets spanning ten centuries, including 24 unpublished poets.

==Media coverage==
The Folch Lab has been featured in ''[[The New York Times]]'' (February 2, 2003, Technology section),<ref name="NYT">{{cite web|date=2003-02-20|title=New York Times article on the Folch lab's microfluidic photomasks|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/02/20/technology/what-s-next-versatile-masks-of-dye-speed-the-chip-making-process.html|access-date=2011-10-25|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> ''[[Science News]]'' (February 15, 2003 issue), ''[[Physics World]]'' (March 2003 issue), ''[[Materials Today]]'' (April 2003 issue), ''[[Photonics Spectra]]'' (April 2003 issue), ''[[BioPhotonics International]]'' (May 2003 issue),<ref>{{cite journal|last=Hogan|first=Hank|url=http://faculty.washington.edu/afolch/_Folch_BiophotonicsInternational.pdf|title=Photolithography goes with the flow|date=May 2003|journal=BioPhotonics International|publisher=Laurin Publishing Company|access-date=2015-11-27}}</ref> ''[[Proto (magazine)|Proto]]'' (Fall 2008 issue), ''[[The Washington Post]]'' (October 28, 2008, Health section),<ref name="WP">{{cite web|date=|title=Washington Post article on the Folch lab's combinatorial micromixer|url=http://faculty.washington.edu/afolch/_Folch_WashingtonPostArticle.html|access-date=2011-10-25|publisher=Faculty.washington.edu}}</ref> [[UWTV]] (January 2012),<ref name=UWTV /> [[NTN24]] (November 2014).<ref name=NTN24 /> New Zealand magazine ''The SpinOff'' (15/2/2017 article),<ref name=":2" /> YouTube interviews by ElveFlow (July 2017)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Folch |first=Albert |date=September 18, 2017 |title=Microfluidics Interview: Albert Folch UW Department of Bioengineering |website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o78IFL0Pi7Q}}</ref> and by BIOS / Frontier Science (December 2021).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Folch |first=Albert |date=Dec 4, 2021 |title=Frontier Science #6 - Advanced Microfluidics✨ w/ Albert Folch - Professor @ UW {{!}} BIOS |website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VTVToEV_25Q}}</ref>
